newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Africa welcomes Western support for peacekeeping.
newsitem.headline: Africa welcomes Western support for peacekeeping.

text.p: The Organisation of African Unity said on Thursday it welcomed pledges from the United States, Britain and France to help it build a solid peacekeeping capacity, but said there must be no strings attached to the aid.

OAU spokesman Ibrahim Dagash told a news briefing at an African foreign ministers' meeting that the three Western powers had recently adopted a common position to assist Africa to establish an effective mechanism for peacekeeping and conflict resolution.
The 53-member OAU has for years talked about establishing such a programme, but has cited lack of finance for its failure to get it off the ground.
"We will have to discuss the programme further...but we accept the offer by these countries but nobody should tell us how we should use the money," Dagash said.

"That is the ministers' position on the issue," he said on the first day of a two-day conference by the African ministers preparing for an OAU summit due to be held in the Zimbabwean capital from June 2.
An African peacekeeping and conflict resolution programme on the troubled continent would complement a similar programme run by the U.N., he said.
